title: Find the program that uses the most CPU
summary: Take a one-time snapshot of the running programs sorted by CPU use, so you can see which one is slowing the computer down. This only reads the list; it does not stop or change anything.

aliases.text: what is slowing down my computer
which program uses the most cpu
linux high cpu usage what process

steps.explain: Show the header and the 10 processes that use the most CPU, highest first. ps lists processes; sort by CPU; head keeps only the first 11 lines.
steps.gui: Open the System Monitor app from the application menu, go to the Processes tab and click the CPU column heading to sort by CPU use.
steps.expect: A header line 'PID COMMAND %CPU', then up to 10 lines. The first line under the header has the highest %CPU value.

alternatives.explain: Show a live-style snapshot from top (one screen, batch mode). The summary lines are at the top, the process table below it is sorted by CPU by default.

steps.explain: Read the list. COMMAND is the program name; %CPU near 100 means one processor core is fully busy with it (above 100 is possible on multi-core systems). Run the step again later to compare, and check which program you started before closing anything.
